commentary.text: I’m placing Red directly in the center to establish an early foothold and support Yellow’s next central advance.
I’m taking a central square immediately, restricting the advanced Red piece while building toward Team B’s center-occupation win.
Yellow takes (4,3), securing a second central square while preserving Red’s tactic of moving to (3,5) next turn to sandwich the Blue piece at (3,4).
I’m staging a Green piece beneath the open central square. This supports entry to (4,4) next turn and prepares a same-color flanking structure against Yellow’s advanced center piece.
Red completes the planned flank from (0,5) to (3,5), sandwiching and capturing Blue at (3,4). This clears a third central square for Team A while retaining Red at (3,3) and Yellow at (4,3).

Red’s capture cost us one Blue piece, so I’m replacing that lost central presence by moving into the other open center square. This also obstructs Yellow’s expansion and gives Team B a durable foothold.

Yellow closes the horizontal flank at (4,5), using Yellow at (4,3) to capture the newly advanced Blue piece on (4,4). This removes a second Blue and preserves Team A’s central foothold; Blue is now one loss from elimination.

I’m placing Green into the vacated center. Because moving into an existing sandwich is safe, this creates a foothold and makes the Yellow piece at (4,3) vulnerable to a Green flanking capture from the left on a later turn.
Red occupies the third central square, tightening Team A’s control. If Green leaves (4,4), Yellow can immediately enter it for center victory; meanwhile Blue remains one capture from elimination.

With Blue one loss from elimination, I’m withdrawing an exposed edge piece into a safer supporting square. From (2,4), it pressures the Red center column and can serve as a future same-color flank for a vertical capture.

I’m withdrawing Yellow from (4,5) to create a decisive center fork. Green at (4,4) cannot remain indefinitely because Yellow can return to (4,5) and sandwich it; if Green vacates the center now, Red can occupy (4,4) on the next turn and complete Team A’s four-square center victory.
Yellow has vacated the right side of the center, completing the Green flanking pattern on the left. I’m closing it now: the move to (4,2) sandwiches Yellow at (4,3) against our Green piece at (4,4).

Red shifts to (4,5) to support a renewed center squeeze. Yellow should next advance from (7,3) to (4,3), restoring three Team A center squares; if Green then vacates (4,4), Red can occupy it for the immediate center win.

I’m shifting Blue’s supporting piece to (2,3), directly above Red’s center occupant. This establishes the far Blue flank for a future vertical sandwich if another Blue can approach the open square at (4,3).
Yellow repositions beneath the open center square, preparing to advance to (4,3) and restore three-square central control while keeping the route clear for a center win.
Yellow’s move to (5,3) offers another sandwich opportunity. I’m moving Green to (5,2), creating one flank; our Green at (4,4) can descend to (5,4) next turn to close the sandwich if Yellow stays put.
Red makes a safe edge development, preserving the central structure while avoiding an uncertain occupied origin.

I’m positioning Blue at (6,3), directly below the contested file. Yellow must soon vacate (5,3) or be sandwiched by Green; once it clears, this Blue can move through to (4,3) and capture Red at (3,3) against our Blue flank at (2,3).
Yellow restores our three-square center occupation and forces Green to keep defending (4,4). Red at (4,5) remains poised to occupy that square immediately if Green vacates it.

Yellow’s escape lands exactly between two available Green flanks. I’m moving the staged Green from (5,2) to (4,2), sandwiching Yellow at (4,3) against Green at (4,4) and reopening Blue’s route up the third column.

Red steps to (4,3), using the Red piece at (4,5) to sandwich and capture Green’s central defender on (4,4). This reopens the center; if Blue occupies the vacated (3,3), Red can later play from (0,2) to (3,2), sandwiching that Blue against Red at (3,4) for Blue’s third loss.

Red disrupted the original Blue route, but its piece at (4,3) can be attacked with a new vertical sandwich. I’m moving Blue to (5,3); next, the Blue at (2,3) can land on (3,3), trapping that Red between the two Blue pieces if it remains.

Yellow occupies (4,4), giving Team A three central squares again. Red controls the remaining route: if Green enters (3,3), Red can flank it from (3,2) against Red at (3,4); otherwise Red can aim to occupy (3,3) and complete the center.

The pieces on row 4 now form a long capturable chain ending at our Green on (4,2). I’m staging Green at (6,6), threatening to rise to (4,6) and sandwich both Red pieces and the nearly eliminated Yellow piece in one sweep.
Red steps from (4,3) to the final open central square, completing Team A’s four-square center occupation for an immediate victory.
Red moved back onto (3,3), completing the vertical Blue sandwich we prepared. I’m advancing the lower Blue to (4,3), capturing that Red against our Blue at (2,3) while also claiming a central square.
Yellow executes a mixed-line sandwich: moving to (4,1) traps Green at (4,2) and Blue at (4,3) against Yellow at (4,4). Both are captured, giving Blue its third loss and eliminating Blue.

With Blue eliminated and Green one loss from elimination, Team A is threatening to fill the center in its next Red–Yellow cycle. I must occupy (3,3) now to break that immediate center-occupation sequence.

Red delivers the decisive capture: moving from (0,2) to (3,2) sandwiches Green at (3,3) against Red at (3,4). This is Green’s third loss, eliminating Green and winning by eliminating both opposing colors.
